top_stories.title: Iran–U.S. ceasefire sends oil tumbling and lifts crypto
points: Bitcoin reclaimed $65,000, up ~1.2% in 24 hours, as the U.S. and Iran held fire for a second day.
Brent crude fell 4.7–7% to roughly $87–92 a barrel; WTI dropped ~5% to about $85, easing inflation pressure.
Ether rose over 3% to nearly $1,950, outperforming bitcoin, while Solana, XRP and other top-10 tokens gained 1–2%.
DeFi tokens led the bounce, with AAVE and LDO up ~9% (DeFi = decentralized finance, lending and trading apps that run on blockchains without banks).
Nasdaq and S&P 500 futures rose ~0.5%; the Australian dollar and euro strengthened against the U.S. dollar.
Bitcoin dominance (bitcoin's share of total crypto market value) held at 58.6%, meaning the altcoin rally is not yet broad-based.

unique_angles.point: Markets still price a 36.3% chance of a 25-basis-point rate hike (a 0.25 percentage point increase in the Fed's benchmark borrowing rate) at the July 28–29 Fed meeting.
Frames the same repricing as odds of a Fed hike this week falling from 37.4% to 30.5%, and ties the oil drop to the Strait of Hormuz standoff.

items.title: $5B of bitcoin call options cluster at $70K–$72K
points: Nearly $5 billion in bitcoin call options (contracts betting the price rises) sits at the $70,000 and $72,000 strikes on Deribit — 18% of all BTC options open interest there.
Calls outnumber puts more than 10-to-1: ~39,000 calls vs 3,800 puts at $70,000, and ~37,900 calls vs 1,200 puts at $72,000.
The dominant trade is a bull call spread — buying the $70,000 call and selling the $72,000 call — making up ~49–50% of call open interest at those strikes.
One trader or group paid $3.4 million in premium for outright $70,000 calls.

Positioning rests on hopes the CLARITY Act (U.S. crypto market-structure bill) passes this month, but Polymarket odds fell from 51% to 38% after Senate Majority Leader Thune said it will miss the August recess.

items.title: EU's 21st Russia sanctions package hits crypto
points: Targets the A7 cross-border payments network, which Chainalysis says has processed ~$120 billion and was built for sanctions evasion, plus its A7A5 stablecoin.
Fourteen crypto service platforms in Georgia, Panama, the UAE, the Marshall Islands, Kyrgyzstan and Belarus are barred from transacting with EU entities.
A new instrument allows a blanket ban on transactions between any EU crypto provider and any crypto service used by Russia — the EU's first full third-country crypto ban option.
Also freezes assets for 94 banks, extends bans to 33 more Russian credit institutions, and hits 40+ shadow-fleet vessels.
Lands three days after Russia's Duma passed its own crypto framework, effective September 1.

items.title: Memecoins fade as institutions move in
points: DOGE and SHIB combined are now worth just 1.02% of bitcoin's market cap, down from 7% at the 2021 peak.

items.title: Morgan Stanley launches spot Ethereum and Solana ETFs
points: Morgan Stanley launched spot Ethereum and Solana ETFs (exchange-traded funds: stock-market-listed baskets that hold the asset directly, so buyers get price exposure without holding crypto), giving wealth-management clients access via ordinary brokerage accounts.
As one of the largest U.S. wealth managers, its approval opens ETH and SOL to advisers who cannot buy tokens on crypto exchanges.
Spot ETFs create structural buying because the fund must purchase and hold the underlying token for every share issued.
Ethereum and Solana are the two most-used smart-contract blockchains (networks that run programmable applications, not just payments), making them the natural next listings after Bitcoin.
The issue carried only the headline and CoinMarketCap boilerplate — no tickers, fee levels or launch-day inflows were disclosed.

items.title: SK Hynix perps flash-crash on Hyperliquid an hour before the stock did
points: SK Hynix perpetual futures (crypto derivatives that track an asset's price with no expiry date) fell 20% to $900 between 23:00 and 23:01 UTC on July 28, recovering above $1,000 within a minute; analysts blamed thin overnight liquidity.
One hour later SK Hynix stock opened down 15% in Korea, with the Kospi off 11% and Samsung and Hyundai also falling — the perps market priced the drop first.

Root cause: Nvidia fell 5% on reports of a $250 billion data-center commitment to an OpenAI-affiliated venture, dragging SK Hynix (a top supplier of high-bandwidth memory chips for AI processors) to a ~48% decline from its June 26 peak.

items.title: Visa launches Stablecoin Platform with Open USD
points: The Visa Stablecoin Platform lets banks and fintechs mint, burn and manage their own stablecoins (crypto tokens pegged 1:1 to a currency like the dollar) in one Visa-run environment, with maker/checker approvals, passkey signing and wallet-as-a-service.
Launch partner is bank-governed Open USD rather than incumbents Circle (USDC) or Tether (USDT).
EY Parthenon found 63% of corporates want stablecoin access through their own bank.
Supported chains are Ethereum, Solana and Tempo; the model mirrors Visa DPS, which lets thousands of card issuers process debit without building infrastructure.

items.title: Bitmine nears 5% of all Ether
points: Bitmine Immersion holds 5.79 million ETH (~4.8% of circulating supply), worth ~$11.3 billion, making it the largest corporate Ether holder among public companies.
Weekly buying accelerated to 9,946 ETH from 7,430 the prior week.

About 85% (4.9 million ETH) is staked via its MAVAN validator network (staking = locking coins to help secure the network in exchange for interest-like rewards), projected at $299 million in annualized rewards at full deployment.

Total assets are $11.8 billion including 208 BTC, $268 million in cash and securities, and stakes in Beast Industries and Eightco; it has repurchased 11.6 million shares since July 1 under a $4 billion buyback.

items.title: Base ships Base Verify Onchain
points: Coinbase's Base blockchain launched Base Verify Onchain, letting apps enforce one-claim-per-real-person for airdrops and voting without exposing users' personal data.

items.title: Neobank audit: 368 firms, 1.46 billion users
points: Asia holds 817 million of 1.46 billion neobank customers; WeBank alone exceeds 400 million and Nubank's 131 million Latin American users outnumber the entire U.S. neobank base, while Revolut's 50 million European accounts look small by comparison.

Only 127 of 368 hold a full banking license; the rest rely on sponsor banks and banking-as-a-service middlemen, whose failures have pushed customers into bankruptcy proceedings instead of deposit insurance when the ledger of whose money was whose broke.
30% of neobanks founded in the 2020s are web3-native self-custodial apps (users hold their own keys) versus 4% of the 2010s cohort.
Only 67 of 368 (18%) have verified production AI deployments, led by thin-file lenders in Nigeria, the Philippines and Mexico.

issues.subject: Morgan Stanley Just Launched Ethereum and Solana ETFs

headlines: Morgan Stanley launched spot Ethereum and Solana ETFs, giving its wealth-management clients regulated exposure to the two largest non-Bitcoin cryptocurrencies through ordinary brokerage accounts.

The move extends major Wall Street crypto product lineups beyond Bitcoin, signalling that altcoin ETFs (exchange-traded funds: stock-market-listed baskets that hold an asset directly, so buyers get price exposure without holding crypto themselves) are now mainstream distribution products.
The newsletter issue itself contained only the headline and CoinMarketCap boilerplate, with no body copy, data tables, or supporting article text to summarize further.

sections.title: What was actually in the issue
points: 1. The email consisted of the subject line 'Morgan Stanley Just Launched Ethereum and Solana ETFs' plus a standard CoinMarketCap intro line and a 29 Jul 2026 11:00 UTC timestamp.
2. No article body, price data, charts, or source links were included in the delivered text, so no figures (fund tickers, fee levels, launch-day inflows) can be reported.
3. Treat the ETF launch as the single confirmed item; any detail beyond 'Morgan Stanley launched Ethereum and Solana ETFs' would require checking CoinMarketCap or the issuer's filings directly.

sections.title: Why the headline still matters
points: 1. Morgan Stanley is one of the largest US wealth managers, so approving Ethereum and Solana ETFs makes those assets available to advisers who cannot buy tokens on crypto exchanges.
2. Ethereum and Solana are the two most-used smart-contract blockchains (networks that run programmable applications, not just payments), making them the natural next ETF listings after Bitcoin.
3. Spot ETFs create steady structural buying because the fund must purchase and hold the underlying token for every share issued.
